Based on the Marital Dissolution Agreement, Grant’s obligation regarding your neck injury medical expenses is limited and not open-ended.

The relevant section says:

> “The parties agree that any future medical issues relating to Wife’s prior cervical spine injury shall be made in good faith. Husband agrees to cover any expenses relating to future medical issues concerning Wife’s prior injury, up to the applicable annual deductible. All additional, non-covered expenses or costs shall be the sole responsibility of Wife.” fileciteturn0file0L?-L?

This means, as written in the agreement:

- He agreed to cover expenses related to your cervical spine injury only up to the annual deductible amount.
- Once the deductible is met for the year, any remaining costs, non-covered treatment, co-insurance, surgery balances, therapy, etc., become your responsibility unless otherwise agreed.
- The agreement does not appear to place a specific end date on this obligation.
- However, it also does not require him to pay unlimited medical costs forever. It is capped at the deductible each applicable year.

Also important:
- The agreement says these future medical issues are to be handled “in good faith,” which is somewhat subjective and can create interpretation disputes.
- The agreement separately states he must maintain your health insurance through the end of 2026. fileciteturn0file0L?-L?
- After 2026, you are responsible for maintaining your own insurance.

One major practical issue is whether your surgery, MRIs, injections, PT, medications, etc. are clearly documented as connected to the “prior cervical spine injury” referenced in the agreement. Your medical timeline and records matter a lot there.

I’m not your attorney, but from the wording alone:
- He likely remains responsible for deductible-level costs tied to the cervical injury while the agreement is in effect.
- He likely is not responsible for all ongoing treatment costs indefinitely beyond that deductible cap.
How long are my neck injury medical bills covered and required to be paid by grant
